results.title: Nomad eSIM - Review 2024 - PCMag Middle East
results.content:
(Credit: Nomad/PCMag)

In the US, Nomad offers six regular plans: 1GB for $4.50 (seven days), 1GB for $6 (seven days), 3GB for $11 (30 days), 5GB for $14 (30 days), 10GB for $24 (30 days), and 20GB for $35 (30 days). Though they offer the same 1GB of data, the $4.50 and $6.00 plans are indeed different. The $4.50 plan supports AT&T and T-Mobile and starts automatically when connected to a network or after a 30-day window. The $6.00 plan is limited to just AT&T but provides a more flexible 60-day activation window.

Nomad also offers shorter day plans ranging from 1 to 10 days that come with 1GB of high-speed data per day plus unlimited data throttled to 512Kbps. The website and app clearly outline each plan’s details, and all listed prices include applicable taxes.

(Credit: Nomad/PCMag) [...] (Credit: Nomad/PCMag)

Nomad's US pricing is in line with other data-only service providers like Airalo and Saily, which charge $4.50 and $4.39, respectively, for 1GB of data over 7 days.

To use Nomad's eSIM service, your device needs to be unlocked and eSIM compatible. Many modern phones, such as the Apple iPhone 16 and the Samsung Galaxy S24, support eSIMs. If you are unsure if your device will work with Nomad, the company lists the phones, tablets, and laptops that are compatible with its service. [...] (Credit: Iyaz Akhtar)

You can view your data usage in the Manage tab of the Nomad app, where you can also see details like when your plan will expire and buy more data. If your data is running low or is set to expire, you will receive a notification. You can purchase additional data at the same price as regular plans. For example, an additional 1GB costs $4.50.

Being a data-only eSIM, you don't get a phone number to call in case there's a network coverage issue and your internet stops working. However, there are options to buy separate voice and text plans. For example, plans for Colombia start at $9, whereas Airalo plans for Colombia start from $4.50.

What I love about this provider is that it doesn't charge you any one-time connection fee or even a fee for the SIM card itself. There's no hidden cost, and you don't have to worry about enormous roaming costs as well. Just pay for the upfront amount of the package, and you’re good to go.

results.content:
A modern travel eSIM for Europe eliminates these issues by offering instant, prepaid mobile data that works across multiple countries, without needing a physical SIM card.

  

This guide compares the most common Europe eSIM providers to help you find the best balance of price, coverage, and reliability.

## What Is an eSIM and How Does It Work in Europe?

An eSIM (embedded SIM) is a digital SIM built directly into your phone. Instead of inserting a plastic card, you install a mobile plan electronically - usually by scanning a QR code or using an app.

  

In Europe, eSIM adoption is particularly strong because:

Saily positions itself as a privacy-focused eSIM provider with both fixed and unlimited data plans for Mexico. Setup happens through the app, and you land connected without manual activation.

Install through the Saily app, choose your Mexico plan, and your connection activates when you arrive.

The process mirrors other app-based providers with one catch: Saily doesn't disclose which Mexican networks it uses, so you can't predict coverage strength before you travel.

As a reseller, Jetpac can't directly troubleshoot network issues if you experience connectivity problems. You're dependent on their relationship with the upstream provider, which creates a longer response chain when things go wrong.

This can be frustrating when you're trying to make a fixed data plan last through your trip.

Saily doesn't offer a free trial, so you're committing before testing the service.

[...] By default, you might just think of using an international version of your existing cellular plan. As a Verizon customer, the international plans they offer for their customers are quite cost-prohibitive. Verizon’s TravelPass is $12/day and while you do get unlimited data, text, and calls, a 17-day trip (which was the duration of my last trip) would cost $204. Other carriers might have more affordable options, but in my case, this is a no-go for me. [...] You’re supposed to be able to check your usage by dialing #123#, but for some reason that wasn’t working for me. Alternatively, I just looked at my cellular settings on my phone to see how much data I had used, so this was a good enough checkpoint for me.

results.title: Buying a SIM Card or eSIM for Travel in Taiwan (2026 Guide)
results.content:
Luckily all of the main companies have booths at Taoyuan airport, so you’ll be able to compare prices at a glance. After you’ve cleared immigration and collected your bags, walk out into the arrivals hall and turn right. Follow the signs for the buses — just before you get to the end of the arrival hall and escalators to take you down to where the buses leave from, you’ll see several booths on your right.

You can get an unlimited 7 day data plan with Chunghwa for 450 NTD (around $13.50 USD). Check what the other companies are offering as well, but that’s not a bad deal. If you don’t need that much data, 1GB costs 180 NTD, and 2.2GB costs 300 NTD, valid for two months.

Hello, [...] |  | Taiwan 70GB - 30 days | 30 days 70GB | $72.50 | | [...] ## Travel eSIM for Taiwan

Compared to buying locally, it’s cheaper to get a travel eSIM unless you really need unlimited amounts of data for your stay. That’s the option I’ve suggested to friends who’ve visited Taiwan in the last couple of years, and they’ve all come back happy with the speeds, service, and (especially) cost.

I’ve found aloSIM to typically have the lowest prices, usually around ten bucks for 10GB of data, with smaller and larger options available. If you don’t need much data, take a look at Instabridge as well: its smaller bundles can be very cheap.

Prices and packages change regularly, of course, so check the table below before making a final decision. The details were last updated on 6 Apr 2026.

Luckily all of the main companies have booths at Taoyuan airport, so you’ll be able to compare prices at a glance. After you’ve cleared immigration and collected your bags, walk out into the arrivals hall and turn right. Follow the signs for the buses — just before you get to the end of the arrival hall and escalators to take you down to where the buses leave from, you’ll see several booths on your right.

You can get an unlimited 7 day data plan with Chunghwa for 450 NTD (around $13.50 USD). Check what the other companies are offering as well, but that’s not a bad deal. If you don’t need that much data, 1GB costs 180 NTD, and 2.2GB costs 300 NTD, valid for two months.

Hello, [...] ## Travel eSIM for Taiwan

Compared to buying locally, it’s cheaper to get a travel eSIM unless you really need unlimited amounts of data for your stay. That’s the option I’ve suggested to friends who’ve visited Taiwan in the last couple of years, and they’ve all come back happy with the speeds, service, and (especially) cost.

I’ve found aloSIM to typically have the lowest prices, usually around ten bucks for 10GB of data, with smaller and larger options available. If you don’t need much data, take a look at Instabridge as well: its smaller bundles can be very cheap.
